{{verse|chapter=14|verse=16}} {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Go{{ls}}pel vpō the 2 Sunday after Penteco{{ls}}t.}}But he {{ls}}aid to him, A certaine man made a great {{ls}}upper, and called many. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=17}} And he {{ls}}ent his {{ls}}eruant at the houre of {{ls}}upper to {{ls}}ay to the inuited, That they {{ls}}hould come, becau{{ls}}e now al things are ready. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=18}} And they began al at once to make excu{{ls}}e. ''Ian. 14.''}}And great multitudes vvent vvith him: and turning, he {{ls}}aid to them, {{verse|chapter=14|verse=26}} {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 10, 37.''}}* If any man come to me and hateth not his {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ No creature {{ls}}o deere vnto vs, vvhich we mu{{ls}}t not hate or for{{ls}}ake, if it hinder vs, and in that re{{ls}}pect that it hindereth vs from Chri{{ls}}t, or his Church, & our Saluation.}}∷ father and mother, and vvife and children, and brethren and {{ls}}i{{ls}}ters, yea and his ovvne life be{{ls}}ides: he can not be my di{{ls}}ciple. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=27}} And he that doth not beare his cro{{ls}}{{ls}}e and come after me: cannot be my di{{ls}}ciple. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=28}} For, vvhich of you minding to build a toure, doth not fir{{ls}}t {{ls}}it dovvne and recken the charges that are nece{{ls}}{{ls}}arie, vvhether he haue to fini{{ls}}h it: {{verse|chapter=14|verse=29}} le{{ls}}t, after that he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to fini{{ls}}h it, al that {{ls}}ee it, begin to mocke him, {{verse|chapter=14|verse=30}} {{ls}}aying, That this man began to build, and he could not fini{{ls}}h it? {{verse|chapter=14|verse=31}} Or<noinclude>{{continues|vvhat}}</noinclude>
